graph.title: LEGO 5970-1 Freeze Ray Frenzy
notes: The 4 separate groups are intentional and not a real problem. The booklet builds four separate models, each with its own parts box and its own numbered steps: the stop sign (p2, b1-b3), the traffic light (p3, b4-b11), the white police hover vehicle (p4-8, b12-b34) and the black jet vehicle (p9-19, b35-b70). No step attaches one model to another, so I kept them as separate components. Adding edges between them would invent connections the booklet does not show.
The cover picture shows the traffic light near the black vehicle, but that is only a display pose. No step attaches it.
Minifigure parts (heads, torsos, legs, helmet, jetpack, neck bracket) are not in the provided parts list, so they are not nodes. The pilots seated on the vehicles are omitted.
Stickers are not parts and are omitted.
The manual is a set of small pictures. Many exact stud positions are inferred, so ports on studs and anti-studs are approximate. The connected piece pairs are the intended ones.
Page 4's 4234006 is a pre-built assembly, shown as b12 (lego-30187b).
Pieces whose catalogue entries lack the needed port (e.g. antenna ends, stud positions on 30187b, the engine's axle hole) use null ports.
The two halves of the black vehicle are joined at the end by pushing axle b56 into engine b35.
The booklet's side-hole bricks are mapped to the catalogue's lego-30414 as listed. Pins and connectors going into side holes use null ports.
The rear 4032a plate (b55) is attached to the cylinder end face via the cylinder's side stud ports. Its axle hole takes the axle.
No repeats are used: the repeated pieces (two curved bricks, two brackets and so on) are placed in different positions, so they do not form identical sub-assemblies.
